# Nodal Framework — coding-agent context

Nodal Framework is a provider-based .NET 10 graph data access framework. Application code models nodes and relationship payloads as POCOs. Nodal.Core owns portable metadata, typed sets, expression translation, canonical results, identity resolution, change tracking, and unit-of-work planning. Nodal.Neo4j and Nodal.TigerGraph compile and execute the portable model through native transports. Nodal.Migrations expresses portable schema intent. Nodal.Analytics is an optional public contract layer for analytics capability integration above the provider boundary. Advanced analytics implementations are outside the public package and documentation contract.

## Installation and host integration

- Install exactly one application provider with `dotnet add package Nodal.Neo4j --prerelease` or `dotnet add package Nodal.TigerGraph --prerelease`.
- Provider packages include `Nodal.Core` transitively. Add `Nodal.Migrations` only when the host owns schema evolution.
- Keep every explicit Nodal package on the same version during the alpha period.
- Register a provider for the application lifetime. Register each `NodalContext` subclass as scoped or create one per explicit unit of work.
- `Neo4jProvider` owns and asynchronously disposes the official pooled Bolt driver. `TigerGraphProvider` consumes an externally managed `HttpClient`.
- Use standard .NET dependency injection; do not generate a new provider per request and do not share one tracked context across concurrent requests.
- Full package and ASP.NET Core examples: https://nodalframework.pages.dev/docs/installation

## Graph analytics

- Start from a typed node query, call `Analyze` with a same-node `RelationSet`, and select a named algorithm such as `PageRank`, `Betweenness`, `Louvain`, or `WeaklyConnectedComponents`.
- Use typed `PageRankOptions` and `LouvainOptions` for stable settings, `OnProjection` for a Neo4j GDS named graph, `WeightedBy` for a mapped numeric relationship property, and `Top` to bound result rows. `WithOption` is reserved for provider-extension parameters.
- `GraphAnalyticsRecord<TNode>` preserves the associated materialized node and every returned metric. `Score` and `CommunityId` are convenience properties; graph- or edge-level algorithms may return no node.
- Neo4j analytics require explicit GDS enablement. TigerGraph analytics require an explicit algorithm-to-installed-query mapping. Unsupported capabilities fail before transport execution.
- The live QA database baselines are Neo4j 5.26 Community and TigerGraph 4.2.4 Community. Neo4j 5.26 requires GDS 2.13. Runtime GDS discovery and projection lifecycle management are implemented; per-algorithm live analytics certification remains deployment-gated.
- Treat compiler verification and live database verification as different guarantees. Consult `/docs/providers/compatibility` before generating provider-specific code.

## Core composition

- Derive an application context from `NodalContext` and pass `IGraphProvider` to its base constructor.
- Expose node sets with `GraphSet<TNode> Property => Set<TNode>()`.
- Expose relationships with `RelationSet<TSource, TRelation, TTarget> Property => Relations<TSource, TRelation, TTarget>()`.
- Apply `[GraphNode]` to node POCOs and `[GraphRelation]` to edge POCOs.
- Apply `[GraphKey]` to a stable domain identifier. `[GraphProperty]` changes the stored property name. `[GraphIgnore]` excludes state.

## Query rules

- Begin with `GraphSet.Query()` or `GraphSet.Match(predicate)`.
- Supported query operations include filtering, ordering, paging, distinctness, projections, bounded terminal operations, and aggregates.
- Traverse typed relations with `Traverse`, `TraverseIncoming`, or path projections with `TraversePath`.
- Reuse hot factories through `NodalCompiledQuery.Compile`.
- Use `Database.QueryRawAsync<T>` only for provider-native operations and always pass values separately as parameters.
- Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only or high-volume work.

## Changes and migrations

- Add/update/remove nodes through `GraphSet` and connect/update/disconnect edge payloads through `RelationSet`.
- Call `SaveChangesAsync` once per bounded unit of work.
- Nodal orders dependencies and accepts tracked state only after provider success.
- Migration classes derive from `NodalMigration`, expose a stable `Id`, and implement `Up` and `Down` with `MigrationBuilder`.

## Provider lifetime

- Keep `Neo4jProvider` long-lived; it owns the official driver's Bolt connection pool.
- Supply TigerGraph with a long-lived, host-managed `HttpClient`.
- TigerGraph administration operations require an `ITigerGraphAdministrativeTransport` appropriate to the deployment.

## Safety constraints

- Do not claim that every graph semantic is portable. Providers reject combinations they cannot preserve correctly.
- Do not parse Neo4j or TigerGraph result formats in application code; use Nodal materialization.
- Do not concatenate user values into native query text.
- Do not place credentials in source, examples, logs, or migration files.
- Treat roadmap items as planned capabilities, not shipped APIs.

## Planned work

- P2 hardens provider certification, samples, migrations, analytics write-back, event/outbox integration, capability metadata, and stable releases.
- `Nodal.Memgraph` and `Nodal.ArangoDB` are provider expansion candidates, not shipped packages.
- Roadmap: https://nodalframework.pages.dev/docs/roadmap

Full guide: https://nodalframework.pages.dev/docs/intro
